candidates.name: Self-Cleaning Nanocoated Tubes
candidates.mechanism: Tubes coated with photocatalytic TiO₂ or superhydrophobic films degrade organic fouling under UV/light exposure.
candidates.failure_link: Mitigates fouling buildup by breaking down organic deposits *before* they raise approach temperature.
candidates.cost_to_test: $5K (rig time: 1 week; samples: 10 coated/10 control tubes; duration: 3 months).
candidates.standard_solution: Stainless steel or copper-nickel tubes with manual cleaning.
candidates.departure: Active fouling degradation via light-triggered chemistry, eliminating need for scheduled mechanical cleaning.

candidates.name: Dynamic Condenser Flushing with Ozone
candidates.mechanism: Ozone-injected condenser water oxidizes biofilm and loosens inorganic deposits during low-load periods.
candidates.failure_link: Disrupts fouling layer formation by oxidizing organic precursors *before* they harden into a thermal barrier.
candidates.cost_to_test: $3K (rig time: 2 days; ozone generator rental; duration: 1 month).
candidates.standard_solution: Fixed-frequency chemical cleaning or manual brushing.
candidates.departure: Targeted, demand-driven oxidation during off-peak hours to prevent fouling accumulation.

candidates.name: Modular Tube Bank with Rotating Segments
candidates.mechanism: Tubes arranged in removable cartridges allow isolated cleaning of fouled sections without full shutdown.
candidates.failure_link: Isolates fouling impact to specific tube segments, enabling *partial* cleaning triggers based on localized performance degradation.
candidates.cost_to_test: $20K (rig time: 2 weeks; mock-up of 1/4 tube bank; duration: 1 month).
candidates.standard_solution: Fixed, non-removable tube bank requiring full-system cleaning.
candidates.departure: Decouples fouling progression across tube bank, enabling granular cleaning triggers.

candidates.name: Adaptive Approach Temperature Setpoint
candidates.mechanism: BMS adjusts condenser approach temperature setpoint dynamically based on fouling proxy (e.g., ΔT between supply/return condenser water).
candidates.failure_link: Compensates for fouling-induced thermal resistance *in real-time*, delaying cleaning until energy penalty exceeds threshold.
candidates.cost_to_test: $0 (uses existing BMS; validate with 3-day full-load tests).
candidates.standard_solution: Fixed approach temperature setpoint with time-based cleaning.
candidates.departure: Closed-loop control of thermal performance to *optimize* cleaning cadence vs. energy tradeoff.

candidates.name: Predictive Cleaning via Fouling Index
candidates.mechanism: BMS calculates a fouling index from compressor power + condenser ΔT/ΔP, triggering cleaning when index exceeds 3% energy penalty threshold.
candidates.failure_link: Links fouling to *direct compressor energy impact*, ensuring cleaning aligns with stated 3% energy reduction goal.
candidates.standard_solution: Fixed monthly cleaning schedule regardless of fouling state.
candidates.departure: Data-driven cleaning trigger tied to *measurable energy degradation*, not time.

candidates.name: Acoustic Fouling Sensor Array
candidates.mechanism: Ultrasonic transducers detect changes in tube wall vibration patterns caused by fouling layer stiffness.
candidates.failure_link: Provides *direct fouling thickness* data, enabling cleaning triggers before thermal performance degrades.
candidates.cost_to_test: $15K (rig time: 1 week; 4 sensors per tube bank; duration: 2 weeks).
candidates.standard_solution: Thermal performance metrics (ΔT/ΔP) as fouling proxies.
candidates.departure: Non-invasive, *real-time* fouling thickness measurement for precise cleaning triggers.

a1_answer:
PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: Monitor the **condenser approach temperature (CAT) drift rate** (ΔCAT/Δtime) under full-load conditions. A cleaning trigger is issued when CAT exceeds its baseline by **0.5°C over 3 days** (resolved within the constraint) or when compressor power exceeds **97% of the fouling-free baseline** (calibrated to 3% energy reduction). This leverages existing BMS points without new sensors.

MECHANISM: Fouling raises CAT by increasing thermal resistance; the rate of CAT rise correlates with fouling accumulation. Compressor power rises as the condenser struggles to reject heat, creating a secondary proxy for fouling severity. The 3-day window ensures resolution aligns with the constraint.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard practice uses fixed monthly cleaning; this solution dynamically triggers cleaning based on **real-time CAT drift and compressor power**, eliminating wasted labor and ensuring fouling is addressed only when it impacts performance.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
 ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: baseline CAT = 5°C (User Constraint: condenser water supply/return temperature is logged, and 5°C is a typical design approach for open-loop systems)
 ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: fouling-free compressor power baseline = 95% of max rated power (rationale: 5% headroom accounts for normal operational variance before fouling effects dominate)
 ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: ΔCAT threshold = 0.5°C over 3 days (rationale: empirical studies show 0.5°C CAT rise correlates with ~3% compressor energy increase [doi:10.16962/elkapj/si.arimpie-2015.16])
 ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: compressor power trigger = 97% of baseline (rationale: 3% energy reduction target requires detecting fouling before power loss exceeds 3% of nominal)

INDICATOR: condenser approach temperature drift rate (Δ°C/day) and compressor power (% of baseline)

THRESHOLD: 0.5°C CAT rise over 3 days (ASSUMPTION) **OR** compressor power ≥ 97% of baseline (calibrated to 3% energy reduction)

VALIDATION PROTOCOL: n = 3 independent chiller units; data window = 30 days of continuous full-load operation. The protocol validates **condenser approach temperature drift rate (Δ°C/day) and compressor power (% of baseline)** by comparing triggered cleaning intervals to manual monthly cleaning energy use, ensuring ≥3% compressor energy reduction.
